title: Pricing + Metering Changes (Q1 2026) — Sales/CS Enablement Deck (DRAFT)
content:
SLIDE 1 — Title
Pricing + Metering Changes (Q1 2026)
Enablement for AEs + CSMs
(DRAFT — not for customer distribution)

Speaker notes:
- This deck covers: (1) what’s changing, (2) what’s not changing, (3) how to talk about it, (4) FAQs + objection handling, and (5) what to do when the console/invoice don’t match.
- Audience: Sales, CS, Solutions Eng (internal use).


SLIDE 2 — Why we’re doing this
What prompted the changes:
- We’re running pricing/packaging experiments (credits, overage tiers, plan gating, Dedicated commit structures).
- We discovered a few meter/accounting edge cases causing confusion (mostly rounding + streaming disconnect handling).
- Goal: make billed usage explainable end-to-end (telemetry → aggregates → invoice) + improve GTM confidence.

What you can say externally:
- “We’re tightening measurement and reporting so usage is more consistent and easier to audit.”
- “We’re improving alignment between the console usage page and invoice line items.”

What you should NOT say externally:
- “We had a billing bug and aren’t sure what happened.”
- Any mention of internal error rates/thresholds unless Finance/Legal approves per account.


SLIDE 3 — What’s changing (high level)
1) Rounding policy alignment
- Invoice aggregation follows the documented rounding decision (ADR-027).
- Removes per-request rounding behavior that could create drift vs. invoice-level totals.

2) Streaming disconnect accounting
- We do not bill tokens generated after the client disconnects.
- Partial usage before disconnect is still billed (what actually streamed / was produced prior to termination).

3) Console usage page alignment
- Time zone normalization and model alias mapping improvements.
- Goal: console totals should match invoice totals for the same window and filters.

4) Better metadata for auditability
- Billing exports include meter_version, aggregation_window, invoice_run_id.


SLIDE 4 — What’s NOT changing
- Meter definitions (tokens, embeddings, rerank units) are the same definitions already documented (v3).
- Hosted API remains usage-based; Dedicated remains contract commit + attribution rules.
- We’re not changing contract terms broadly (any updates go through Legal + PM-614).


SLIDE 5 — Who is impacted (so you can preempt questions)
Most likely to notice a difference:
- Customers with heavy streaming usage (long responses, flaky client connections).
- Customers with high request counts and small per-request usage (historically more sensitive to rounding artifacts).
- Customers comparing:
  - Console “Usage” page totals vs invoice totals
  - Invoice totals vs self-instrumented token counters

Least likely to notice:
- Batch jobs with long contexts where rounding effects are negligible.
- Customers who only review invoice totals, not per-request/stream event logs.


SLIDE 6 — Experiment context (AEs/CSMs: how to message)
We may be in an active experiment for:
- Free credits structure (signup credits, monthly credits, credit expiration rules)
- Overage tiers and effective unit pricing at volume
- Plan gating (features like retention, advanced observability, higher rate limits)
- Dedicated commit structure and burst policies

Approved messaging:
- “You may see different plans/prices depending on eligibility. We’ll confirm your current plan and quote in writing.”
- “If you’re in a test, we can provide a clean ‘control-equivalent’ quote for procurement comparisons.”

Quoting rule of thumb (until further notice):
- Always attach a dated quote summary AND link to the current internal experiment catalog entry (do not forward the internal doc).
- If customer asks “will this price change next month?”, route to Sales Ops + Finance for confirmation before committing.


SLIDE 7 — Metering basics (Hosted API)
Core meters you’ll see on invoices:
- Input tokens (prompt tokens)
- Output tokens (completion tokens)
- Cached tokens (if applicable — billed per plan rules; clarify “cached” ≠ “free”)
- Embeddings units (per input size / embedding vector generation)
- Rerank units (per document scored / request type)
- Requests (if applicable to plan; not always a billed meter)

One-liners:
- “Tokens are the units of text processed by the model.”
- “Input tokens are what you send; output tokens are what the model generates.”
- “Streaming doesn’t change the amount of computation; it changes how results are delivered.”


SLIDE 8 — Metering basics (Dedicated)
What customers pay for:
- Reserved capacity commit (contracted monthly/annual)
- Usage attribution (how requests burn down commit depending on model/throughput profile)

Common confusion:
- “Why does my burn-down not equal the invoice line by line?”
  - Because Dedicated may attribute usage with a capacity model (e.g., reserved throughput time, model profile) rather than strictly tokens.

Approved response:
- “Dedicated usage is attributed per the capacity profile defined in the order form; we can walk through a sample week and show how it maps.”

Action item:
- If Dedicated customer requests changes to commit/burst, loop in Sales Ops + FP&A (Rishi) for margin guardrails.


SLIDE 9 — The one diagram (how billing works)
Telemetry → Aggregation → Invoice
- Raw events: request start/end, token counts, model, region, endpoint type, outcome
- Billing-ready aggregates: grouped by account, model, region, endpoint, time window, meter_version
- Invoice line items: mapped from aggregates + contract pricing rules

What to emphasize:
- “Every billed unit can be traced back to raw telemetry with a documented transformation.”


SLIDE 10 — Console vs Invoice: what customers should expect
Expectation we’re setting internally:
- Same date range + same account + same model filters → console usage should match invoice within normal timing constraints.

Known reasons for mismatch (customer-friendly framing):
- Timing: console may be near-real-time; invoice is finalized after the billing run.
- Filters: model aliases, regions, or endpoints may be grouped differently.
- Windowing: invoice uses a strict billing window; console may default to local time zone.
- Streaming: disconnect handling (now fixed going forward) could affect historical periods.

If a customer reports a mismatch:
- Do NOT speculate on root cause.
- Use the triage flow (see “Billing discrepancy runbook”).


SLIDE 11 — Example: invoice line items (Hosted API)
(Example only — numbers made up)
Invoice section: Hosted API Usage — Jan 2026
- Model: rw-chat-3 (alias of llama-based family)
  - Input tokens: 120,000,000
  - Output tokens: 95,000,000
  - Cached tokens: 30,000,000
- Embeddings (rw-embed-2)
  - Embedding units: 14,500,000
- Rerank (rw-rerank-1)
  - Rerank units: 2,200,000

How to explain:
- “Line items separate by endpoint type and model family so costs are attributable.”
- “If you want, we can provide a usage export keyed by model/region.”


SLIDE 12 — Example: streaming scenario
Customer asks: “If a user closes the browser mid-stream, do we pay for the full response?”
Answer:
- “You’re billed for tokens actually generated up to the disconnect. Tokens that would have been generated after disconnect aren’t billed.”

If they push:
- “We can share request-level logs for a sample set via Support to validate the accounting.”

Internal notes:
- This aligns to ADR-027 and the streaming disconnect fix PR (PR 41903).


SLIDE 13 — Talk track: positioning the changes
Primary positioning (AEs + CSMs):
- Reliability and trust: “We’re making usage reporting more consistent and audit-friendly.”
- Operational clarity: “Invoices map cleanly to meters and the console.”
- No surprise bills: “We’ve tightened how retries/streams are accounted for to prevent confusion.”

Secondary positioning (for technical buyers):
- “We’ve improved observability and added better metadata for auditability (meter_version, invoice_run_id).”


SLIDE 14 — Objection handling #1: “Your token counts don’t match ours”
What’s usually happening:
- Different tokenizers / libraries
- Counting characters/words instead of tokens
- Including client-side retries or excluding server-side retries
- Counting tokens that never reached the model due to validation failures

Approved response:
- “Tokenization can differ across libraries. We bill using the model’s tokenizer and the server-side metering. If you share a sample prompt/response ID, we’ll reconcile together.”

Next step:
- Request artifacts (see runbook): request_ids, time window, model name, region, export if available.


SLIDE 15 — Objection handling #2: “Your console says X but invoice says Y”
Approved response:
- “The invoice reflects the finalized billing window and contract pricing rules. The console is designed to match, but differences can occur due to timing, filters, or windowing. We’ll reconcile this with you.”

Internal do/don’t:
- Do: ask for screenshots + exact filters + time zone.
- Don’t: promise an immediate credit before investigation.

Escalation:
- Support ticket + tag Billing Discrepancy; include impact estimate.


SLIDE 16 — Objection handling #3: “Are you charging us for failed requests/retries?”
Approved response:
- “In general, you’re billed for successful processing. Some retry behaviors can still incur compute; if you believe you’re being billed incorrectly, we can investigate with request outcomes.”

Internal note:
- Telemetry is adding better separation via request_outcome/retry_reason dimensions (ENG-4823 / PR 41917) to make this easier to explain.


SLIDE 17 — Pricing experiments: how to quote safely
Rules (until the quarter closes):
1) Confirm whether the account is in an experiment (ask Sales Ops).
2) Always quote using the approved SKU set and current price book.
3) If credits are involved, specify:
   - credit amount
   - expiration
   - whether credits apply before discounts
   - what happens when credits are exhausted (overage pricing)
4) Put the “measurement and billing” language in front of procurement early for regulated customers.

If procurement requests MFN / price lock:
- Escalate to Sales Ops + Legal; do not agree verbally.


SLIDE 18 — Customer FAQ (short answers)
Q: “Do cached tokens cost less?”
A: “They can, depending on plan/pricing rules. Cached tokens represent repeated prefixes/contexts; we’ll show you how they’re billed on your plan.”

Q: “Is streaming cheaper?”
A: “Not inherently. Streaming changes delivery; cost is driven by tokens and model.”

Q: “Can we set hard spend limits?”
A: “We support quotas/rate limits; CS can help set guardrails.”

Q: “Can we audit usage?”
A: “We can provide exports and documentation; audit rights and dispute windows depend on your contract.”


SLIDE 19 — Billing dispute process (what AEs/CSMs should do)
When a customer disputes usage:
1) Acknowledge and collect required details (time window, invoice number, suspected endpoint/model, examples).
2) Open/attach to Support ticket (Billing Discrepancy).
3) Finance + Telemetry investigate; Sales/CS updates customer with timeline.

What NOT to do:
- Don’t offer credits/refunds without the approval path.

Approval path (summary):
- Small goodwill credits: per Support/CS policy (if applicable)
- Confirmed metering defect credits/refunds: Finance approval (Laura/Emily) + documented root cause + prevention plan


SLIDE 20 — Email templates (internal drafts)
Template A: “We’re investigating”
- Confirm receipt
- Request artifacts
- Provide ETA for next update (e.g., 2 business days)

Template B: “Explained mismatch (no defect)”
- Clarify windowing/time zone/tokenization
- Provide reconciliation summary
- Offer a working session

Template C: “Confirmed defect + remediation”
- Acknowledge issue
- Explain scope and fix window in plain language
- Outline credit/refund and prevention controls


SLIDE 21 — What Sales/CS should memorize (3 bullets)
- Always anchor on: “Billed usage is traceable from raw telemetry and documented meter definitions.”
- Don’t speculate; use the runbook and bring Finance/Telemetry in early when $ impact is non-trivial.
- Experiments: confirm eligibility + get the quote in writing with credit/overage details.


SLIDE 22 — Links + owners (internal)
Primary docs:
- Hosted API meter definitions (v3)
- Invoice line-item mapping to telemetry
- Billing discrepancy triage runbook
- ADR-027 rounding + streaming accounting

Owners / escalation:

- Add a Dedicated attribution worked example (needs a sanitized real account).
